question: A train having length 330 meters takes 11 second to cross a 550 meters long bridge. How much time will the train take to cross a 570 meters long bridge?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance (1) = 330 + 550 = 880 m → 11 s.

Total distance (2) = 330 + 570 = 900 m.

Time = (900 × 11) ÷ 880 = 900 ÷ 80 = 45/4 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is (45/4) seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Train length = 330 m, Bridge₁ = 550 m, Bridge₂ = 570 m, Time₁ = 11 s.

Formula Used: Speed = (Length of Train + Length of Object) ÷ Time

 
 Train
 330 m

 550 m

 Total Dist = 880 m (Case 1)
 Time taken = 11 seconds

⇒ Total Distance₁ = 330 + 550 = 880 m.

⇒ Speed of train = Total Distance₁ ÷ Time₁ = 880 ÷ 11 = 80 m/s.

⇒ Total Distance₂ = 330 + 570 = 900 m.

⇒ Time₂ = Total Distance₂ ÷ Speed = 900 ÷ 80.

⇒ Time₂ = 45/4 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is (45/4) seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two trains of lengths L₁ and L₂ cross each other, total distance is always L₁ + L₂. Relative speed is S₁ + S₂ (opposite) or S₁ − S₂ (same direction).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train crossing a stationary point

When a train crosses a pole, tree, or man, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train itself.</p
